title: patch_file fails on single-object JSON signal files
description: patch_file returned 'error applying hunk' when attempting to update two fields in a well-formed single-object JSON signal file. The context lines and removed lines in the diff matched the file content as returned by read_file, yet the tool rejected both attempts. The fallback write_file path was used successfully. This suggests patch_file may have a line-number or whitespace sensitivity issue with files whose prior read was via a cache-hit response.
proposed_resolution: Investigate whether patch_file uses a different internal normalisation (e.g. CRLF vs LF, trailing newline) than read_file on Windows. Add an integration test: write a known JSON file, read it via read_file, construct a diff updating a field, and assert patch_file applies it without error.

title: fix_signal skill has no moeb tool for loading deferred schemas or retrieving large persisted output
description: The fix_signal MCP tool returns its skill prompt as an 85 KB payload which the harness stores to disk rather than inlining. The agent must use external Claude Code tools (ToolSearch, Bash, Read) to load deferred tool schemas and retrieve the persisted output, violating the moeb-tool-origin rubric. No moeb tool exists for either operation.
proposed_resolution: Add a moeb tool (e.g. get_run_prompt) that retrieves the persisted skill prompt for a given run_id from the harness output store, eliminating the need for external Bash/Read access. Alternatively, have fix_signal return a summary with the run_id and a path to the skill file, and provide a moeb read_file path the agent can use directly. For schema loading, consider whether fix_signal can pre-load required tool schemas in the initial response.

title: complete_review returns no-op for write_file calls not pre-registered in pending_reviews
description: When write_file is used directly (rather than through a path pre-registered by the kernel as requiring review), complete_review returns 'not in pending_reviews (no-op)'. This means the kernel cannot enforce write-review-compliance for writes that go through the fallback write_file path in Phase 3 or for event artifact writes in Phase 5. The review sub-loop still executes correctly in skill logic, but the kernel-side obligation tracking is bypassed.
proposed_resolution: Consider whether write_file should automatically register its path in pending_reviews upon successful write, so that complete_review always has a matching obligation to clear regardless of which code path triggered the write.

title: fix_signal should support catalogue signals in .signal.json (singular) format
description: Phase 1 of fix_signal.skill.md scans for files ending with '.signals.json' (plural, array format). Catalogue signals use the '.signal.json' (singular, single-object format) naming convention. A direct signal_id invocation bypasses Phase 1, so this run succeeded, but an unprompted fix_signal scan would miss all catalogue signals entirely.
proposed_resolution: Update Phase 1 of fix_signal.skill.md to also scan for files ending with '.signal.json' in .moeb/signals/catalogue/, treating each as a single-signal source. Alternatively, normalise all signal storage to one format and migrate catalogue files accordingly.
